transcript:
Marc Spezialy
CFO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Hi, and welcome to Pure Cycle Corporation's first quarter 2026 earnings call. We've had a great start to the year, and we're excited to share with you guys our results for first quarter. A couple of housekeeping notes: the earnings presentation is on our website, so if you're listening on a phone or on replay, you can download the slides from our website. Also, we ask that you stay muted until our Q&A session. With that, I will turn over the call to our President and CEO, Mark Harding.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Thank you, Marc, and I'll add my welcome. As Marc foreshadowed, we've had a very good first quarter. Typically, our first quarter's usually a little more challenging just because of weather issues. For those of you that are watching for ski reservations, we've had a pretty dry year and a good weather year, so it's allowed us to really advance a lot of our construction projects out at Sky Ranch. With that, let me go ahead and start the presentation. Our first slide is always our forward-looking statement, which includes the fact that statements are not historical facts containing reference in this corporation or forward-looking statements. I'm sure most of you are familiar with our forward-looking statements qualifier.
Always want to give a shout-out to our management team, and here with me is Marc Spezialy, as well as Cyrena Finnegan, our controller, in the event that they have any specific questions that they might be able to weigh in on. A great team of professionals that continue to really provide leadership to the company in really all segments of what it is that we're doing, as well as our board of directors. We have a terrific board, a very heavyweight board for a company our size, and all are really engaged and provide significant contributions to the company. I want to give a shout-out to our team and let you know their continued support and engagement. As most of you know, this is just a quick investment snapshot.
We've got a continuing streak of profitable quarters, so we're very thrilled that we continue to deliver profitability and shareholder value. We operate in all three business segments: land development, water utilities, and single-family rentals, and they're all doing great. We have good visibility with our land development. We're really striving to continue to develop and build our recurring revenue base. Our great balance sheet; we continue to build, fortify our strong balance sheet, and continue investing in our business lines, as well as grow the business and create shareholder value. Really a solid diversification of the company's activities. Let me jump into the quarter results. As you see from a revenue side, great quarter on the revenue. Q1, really, I think it was a record-setting Q1 for us just because of the seasonality issues.
What we really see on the highlights are we brought in two new home builders to our portfolio that are really engaged in phase IID, which is what we're working on. We punched out completion of phase IIC at the end of our fiscal year last year and continuing through with phase IID. We'll talk a little bit more about IIE coming up. Due to the weather, we were able to get a lot of the curbs and even asphalt down in the November-December timeframe, which is really unheard of here. We're about 80% done with the roads in IID, and that's about five or six months ahead of schedule. Really capitalizing on the weather, and we really kept our contractors engaged on the site so that as we continued to have that weather, we were able to capitalize on that.
Moving over to the profitability side, net income and earnings per share: significant increases in net income and earnings per share. That's a result of the progress on phase IID. You see a significant uptick in both of those. We're very pleased to be able to continue to deliver those results and streamline our revenues throughout the year. This would be a more typical even flow of those earnings and those revenue streams. With the seasonality, we have those variability factors. Through the first quarter, we achieved about a third of our fiscal year forecast. We're ahead of schedule on what our guidance was. Take a look at that great start, bringing in a little over $9 million in revenue and then about $6.2 million in gross profits. Terrific results from our management team, our operators, and folks in the field.
Year-to-date results, net income, earnings per share, similarly, we're ahead of our guidance. We've got about 37% of our full-year guidance on that. Terrific opportunity to continue to deliver that. Really moving forward from how we're looking at developing the land side of it, really being able to be in a position to deliver more results on phase IIE, continuing to produce those lots for our home-builder customers. Really want to take those results and parse those out a little bit for everyone so we can separate that out into the three segments and show you what the contributions are for each of those segments, breaking them down into the water utility segment.
As most of you are familiar with, we really have two revenue sources, two classes of customers. We have our domestic customers, which is where we deliver water and wastewater to residential units. Those are our customers that are at Sky Ranch. They're at other projects that we provide water service to in other areas. We have our industrial customers where we provide water to the oil and gas industry primarily for fracking wells that they're drilling in and around mostly Arapahoe County. We have done wells in other counties, but the bulk of our activity really centers around Arapahoe County and the Lowry Ranch, which is our service area. In those revenues, in the water and the wastewater side, we kind of have two different forms of revenues. We have the recurring monthly revenues where we're doing that on a meter basis.
We also have the capital component of that, which are connections, which are really connecting to our water system from our home-builder customers, our homes, businesses, to each individual system connection and those are through the form of tap fees. They're high capital costs, which are usually incorporated into a mortgage or the development of that business and so those are the two revenue streams attributable to that. When you parse out that data, we continue to see strong customer growth of the recurring revenue. We get a 22% customer CAGR, so we're very pleased about continuing to grow that recurring revenue. While we had a record quarter overall, the water segment, a little bit softer than normal.
That was primarily attributable to just the timing of getting building permits, getting some of those tap fees, and then also taking a gap in the oil and gas deliveries. We had our oil and gas operators concentrating on building a portfolio of well permits. We'll see that tick up the rest of the year. We've got a number of wells that have been drilled and completed, and then they're just starting fracking later this month. They'll be fracking most of the year. You're going to see a substantial uptick in that. You take a look at that in comparative quarters through the last couple of years. That shows you really the variability of the oil and gas side, but we do expect that to tick up for the rest of the year.
Taking a look at that one specific industry on the oil and gas side, they fluctuate. That, as I said, it really is a function of permits and getting the sites constructed. They're building these large multi-well pad sites that will have somewhere between 10 and 20 wells on each of these pad sites. They're really concentrating their activity to a pad site, and they have the directional drilling on these pad sites. As you see some of the trending in that, this is an annual snapshot of how we look for oil and gas revenues. As an illustration in 2024, they were pretty evenly distributed throughout the quarters. I think you're going to start to see a little bit of that similar activity of the quarterly distribution for the rest of the quarters for us in fiscal 2026.
What we do like to do is give you a feel for capacity, how much water is available for our high-volume customers, like the oil and gas customers, as well as where we're at on continuing to invest into the company's assets. What we like to try to do is make sure that we have a steady pace of investment in water and wastewater infrastructure for our customers and balance that out with the need for that portfolio. This shows you we do have a substantial amount of capacity that we've invested in. If you took a look at it just for the quarterly area, really didn't use all that much of it just because of that oil and gas variability. We're really only using about 3% of our overall water portfolio.
Taking a look at the capacity that we have for annual production, we can produce about 2,800 acre-feet. We really only used about 150 acre-feet of that. It does give you a sense of what the pedal strength is on our water portfolio and our water system. Let's take a look at our land development segment. This aerial shot is illustrative of the high school that is under construction. We're very pleased to see that being coming out of the ground, and that will be completed in time for our kids for the fall of 2026. In our land development segment, you've heard us talk a lot about the various phases. Phase IIC, which we did complete last fiscal year, we're midway, a little bit more than midway on phase IID.
We have a percent completion methodology for how we recognize revenue on that, continued lot protection for phase IID, and then also moving into phase IIE, which would be about another 160 lots. We'll start grading on that sometime in this March timeframe. Really enjoying some of that good weather so that we can continue to do some of that pavement, curbs, and gutters for delivering those lots. If you take a look at the lot development revenue, this is really where the strength of the quarter came from, is really building into that phase IID. We're complete with phase IIC, really highlighting some of this. If you want to take a look at the number of homes that are being built, and that's really kind of a function of the housing market.
I know there's a lot of press out there about the housing market and the strength of the housing market and how interest rates are impacting that. We're seeing substantial continued support for what it is that we're doing. I think that's largely indicative of our market segmentation as an entry-level product. Taking a look at the homes complete or under construction in phase IIB, which is really going to balance out the inventory for each of our home builders out at the project. We've got about 85% of phase IIB completely built out. Taking a look at phase IIC, which is what we just delivered, we have one of our newer home builders going vertical with a strong portion of their portfolio. We even have one of our new builders into the portfolio already starting homes in phase IID.
Even though we haven't fully completed IID, we have completed enough of much of that infrastructure where we've got all the water, sewer, storm, curbs, and gutters, and access for that for them to start in IID before we deliver all of those finished lots. What you're seeing is we typically had annual lot deliveries for what was a portfolio of four builders. They try and manage out that inventory so that they don't take any more inventory than what they foresee is for an annual year of production. As the market slowed, what we saw was that there was availability for other builders in there. We moved our portfolio up to seven national home builders working on that. That gives us a strong portfolio of builders that each of them are continuing to maintain their desired level of inventories.
We can continue to pace our development of the project so that we're continuing to accelerate the monetization of the land side. This is an illustration of the snapshot, a visual snapshot of each of the phases from the sub-phases from phase II here. Some nice aerials, which have activities, each of our entry-level segmentations on these. A lot of product diversity where we have a 35-feet lot, 40-feet lot, 45-feet lot on the standard detached. We have segmentation into paired product, which is a townhome product, I'm sorry, a duplex product, and then also townhome products that really offer a variety of price points for this entry-level market. The land development timeline, this is an illustration of how we do the accounting for that. There's three basic phases that we deliver lots to our home builder customers.
That's at a plat where you've got a severable title instrument to the individual lot. We typically get 1/3 of our revenue for the lot payment on that then we do the grading and wet utilities with that money to deliver that progress payment. Finally, moving into the roads, curbs, and gutters to get the finished lot payment. That shows you a phasing of that. It really shows you how we layer in the phasing by quarters. Really, I think the key area for us this year was being able to really substantially do a bunch of finished lots in this Q2, which typically doesn't happen for us just because of the seasonality. Want to really talk a little bit. We were able to expand and amend our interchange access permit with CDOT and really got us another phase.
We've been talking about a lot of these sub-phases for two, which started out as about 850 lots. I think we have the flexibility to get about another 180 lots in there. This phase IIE is about 159 lots. This gives you an aerial of where that's going to look. It's right across the street from the school there. We'll start grading this spring, and you're going to start to see a bit more overlap in that chart we had before on how we deliver those lots to our home builder customers. As I mentioned, the key milestone was the start of construction of the high school. This gives us a full K-12 campus on site, which is very. It's a high advantage.
Most of our home builder customers, really, in the feedback that they're getting from their purchasers, the school is one of the key elements that are driving people to Sky Ranch. Just because it's a local school, it's walkable for everybody. It's a terrific asset for us. What we always like to highlight is some of the key areas of where the Denver metropolitan area is growing and gives you a perspective. I think this is a graphic that many of you have seen before, but it gives you the fact that we really grow one direction. We can't grow west just because of the mountains. We find ourselves in really the most attractive sub-market of the Denver metropolitan area along the I-70 corridor.
If you're looking at the mapping on the right of this illustration, that black line at the top is the interstate. I-70 shows you where Sky Ranch is positioned on that. The pink area is really our service area at the Lowry Ranch. What you're seeing is more and more development occurring around the borders of the Lowry Ranch. We're excited about continuing to expand our operations out at the Lowry property as the state of Colorado determines what it is that they're looking for and how they'd like to monetize that asset for the school trust. I want to give you an update on the single-family rental segment. We've got 19 homes now completed and all rented. That segment continues to drive recurring revenues. We've got another 40 units under contract.
What we're trying to do is phase how those really hit the market. We're trying to phase those at around four or five units coming online each month. That'll start beginning in May and then bringing those units online so that we make sure that we can get them leased and continue to really offer an opportunity for those who are looking for a house but are running into the affordability challenges. That continues to be one of the key issues in the housing market, the affordability. Taking a look at some of the individual performance on their continued growth in the rentals, that's because adding more units online as well as capital appreciation of those assets is a very tax-advantaged segment for us because we retain the equity of the lot and the water service connections in there.
Those houses continue to grow in value as we continue to add value to the overall community. A little bit about the phasing of how we're looking at bringing these units online for each of these different phases from the first phase one, which we completed several years ago, up through what we're looking for in IIE. Bringing online about 100 units for that. I'll talk a little bit about our capital allocation and how we're building that continued shareholder value. Really want to emphasize each of these segments, the water segment where we're growing assets in each of these segments through investing in them, whether we're investing into the brick and mortar of the land segment, whether we're investing into pumps and pipes and diversion structures for our water segment, and then building our home inventory for single-family liquidity.
We continue to grow the balance sheet in all three of these segments. Then really take a look at protecting and preserving the balance sheet so that we can have that liquidity for continuing to invest in each business segment and deliver recurring revenues for our customers. How that looks, we drive shareholder returns through those recurring revenues and water single-family units, and a diversified mix of revenue from tap fees to industrial water fees. We have oil and gas royalties, which were substantially, they were very strong last year. We continue to build our earnings. Really, each of these segments build value from each other. There's a vertical integration in some of those segments that give us where we add value to one, we're adding value to all.
Shareholder values reiterate our fiscal year guidance as well as give you some interim and build-out forecast revenues for our asset growth. When you take a look at the segments of the revenues, the water recurring revenues, as well as single-family rental revenues, gives you a snapshot of how we're building that through the portfolio as well as what that asset growth is. We've talked substantially about bringing on that asset value from Sky Ranch, building out the rest of the residential projects as well as the commercial projects. Great opportunities, and we continue to execute on that. Trending, this illustrates the profitability trend and our fiscal year guidance and the near-term outlook. Again, we want to stay on pace with that. We've had a great quarter on delivering ahead of schedule and had results on fiscal 2026.
This shows you, as we get that interchange constructed, how we look to open up and unlock the balance of the portfolio value. Valuation and sensitivities, our fiscal year guidance was in that $26 million-$30 million range. Earnings per share, $0.43-$0.52 per share. The upside in the timing acceleration for delivering some of those lots and how we might continue that trend. Continuing to reinvest in ourselves with our share buyback program and balance the liquidity needs of the company, and how we're investing into each of our land assets against what we continue to believe is an undervaluation of the company's current trading price. What I also wanted to do, a bit of a new slide this quarter and really illustrate.
You've heard us talk about the interchange, its importance, and kind of how it's phasing. What we're looking to do is get that permit finalized with the county and CDOT sometime early half of this year. Then really take a look at the bonding opportunities with some mill levies that we've reserved at the project and start construction on that in 2027. This is what it looks like and how it's going to orientate to the overall development. The existing interchange will go away. We'll realign that along the section line and give it a diamond interchange capacity here. This is obviously an important component for us to continue to build into phase three as well as bringing online the commercial opportunities for that.
Taking a look at a little bit longer range outlook, the commercial parcels really provide a lot of the high-value land and a lot of the AV. That assessed value is really where the public improvement reimbursables get their strength from us not having to advance those funds, getting reimbursed. I think our receivable on that's currently around $50 million. The combination of the assessed value, Colorado is what we define as a sales tax incentive state. We get literally four times the tax revenues from commercial assessed value as we do residential assessed value. In this particular case, we get public improvement fees on that, which is really a sales tax receipt on that. Those two are significant revenue drivers. This gives you a feel for some of the land planning that we're doing there with some grocery anchors.
Taking a look at a Flex building structure like this, where what we're looking at is maybe offering opportunities for us to partner with others that might be high water users. Some of the current activity, we've engaged local real estate, commercial, industrial real estate brokers that are very active in data centers. We have a very unique opportunity here at Sky Ranch and together with Pure Cycle, given the fact that we have a high availability of water.
We can really distinguish ourselves for these high water use and high water intensive type users. We'll see how that develops over the next few months, year or so. With that, those are our prepared remarks. Maybe what we can do is open it up to some questions and get a little bit of color if you'd like on how things are rolling along. If you're on mute or if you're not on mute, and you've been quiet, thank you. Just go ahead and shout out. If you've got a question, we'll try and give you some detail.
[Unknown Speaker 1]
Unknown Speaker 1
Mark?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Yes, Elliot.
[Unknown Speaker 1]
Unknown Speaker 1
Good morning. Very interesting to see you put the estimates of earnings out there. There was one pretty obvious blank, and that was for fiscal 2027. What should we be thinking about in terms of estimated earnings range for fiscal 2027?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Good question. 2027 is going to be a large component of phase IIE. Taking a look at how we roll into some of the interstate construction and some of the other segments. I think it's going to look a lot like the last couple of years. There's not going to be a real breakout year in 2027, but we really think that breakout year is going to be more once we get the interchange complete and get that commercial online and into development. There are opportunities to do non-high traffic commercial users out there that we're marketing to. As we continue to grow traffic, we have that obligation to continue to build that infrastructure.
[Unknown Speaker 1]
Unknown Speaker 1
Probably $0.75 a share is too high for fiscal 2027 is what I think you're saying.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Yeah. I wouldn't say that that would be a good clear guidance. When we take a look at that commercial and bringing on that in that 2028 timeframe, you really do supercharge because what we're really going to see, we're going to see delivery of lots on the residential side. We think we double up on that revenue stream on the delivery lots on the commercial side.
[Unknown Speaker 1]
Unknown Speaker 1
Refresh my mind. I can't remember whether on taps sold, the pre-tax margin is 50% or 60%. Which is it?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
That's a great question. When we look at it on the aggregate, if you look at the build-out of what will be 60,000 units of it, we believe that margin's around 50% because we have to continue to build that system. In a more short-term basis, I think we're seeing a lot more margin on those because we kept ahead on developing capacity on that. When we're looking at year over year in the last couple of years and the next couple of years, those margins might be a little bit higher on that. When we look at it on an average build-out, if you take $40,000 applied to 60,000 taps, that $2.4 billion revenue potential on that, that's usually about. It's going to cost us about $1.2 billion to build that system out. I think near-term, because we have that excess capacity, those actual realized margins are going to be higher than that 50%.
[Unknown Speaker 1]
Unknown Speaker 1
When you in the past have talked about we're going to have to spend $1 billion, that $1 billion, is it amortized in the cost? When is the 50% pre-tax margin after including amortization of that billion dollars that you talk about? That's included.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Yes. It is included.
[Unknown Speaker 1]
Unknown Speaker 1
Thank you very much.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
You bet.

Unknown Speaker 2
Mark, Tucker Anderson, can you hear me?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
I can, Tucker. Nice to hear from you.
[Unknown Speaker 2]
Unknown Speaker 2
First, I'd like to take a minute, as long as you guys were nice enough to provide it, to shout out hello to my old friend Elliot Knight. Anyways, a couple of questions. First, what do you see as the opportunities for water acquisition at this point? As you talked about in the past, you're always on the lookout for adding to your water acquisition and opportunities for utilizing that water. Could you talk about that broadly?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
You bet. I'd say we've got a very strong water portfolio right now. When we take a look at water acquisitions, because we always do, and one of the ones that folks are constantly knocking on doors with projects, I think we're content with where our portfolio is today. Our acquisitions are really going to be strategic where they are adjacent to our existing portfolio. They provide the most economies of adding to it and the synergies around where we've got our investments today. I would say our appetite for water acquisitions is probably it has to be the right water. It has to be in the right location. I'd say we're more cautious about water acquisitions than I think we would otherwise be in maybe some of the other areas like land.
We'd be more aggressive on land acquisitions than water acquisitions right now just because we want more portfolio on vertically integrating that value because where we buy that land, we have water that we can serve it. We have infrastructure that's there that we can serve it. Building into the land portfolio and then single-family rental portfolio, that drives all three segments where a water acquisition would be nice. It will be valuable because we're not making any more. In fact, it's getting drier and drier. The existing water rights continue to illustrate value. It's a bit, we already have deep portfolio there. Tucker, I would say they have to be the right water right in the right location.
[Unknown Speaker 2]
Unknown Speaker 2
You've just segued into the next topic on my question list here and that is what's happening in the area of land acquisitions given the tension between home building having slowed down substantially, but you still being in a fairly rapidly growing area where, as you pointed out, you can only grow in so many directions. Are you more optimistic, less optimistic, or the same in terms of your potential for land acquisitions?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
I'm more optimistic. I'd say conversations that we've had with the landowners through the years, and where they were previously to where they are today, are much more interesting and much more active. I would say I'm more optimistic about where that sits for us to expand our portfolio and really show a stronger runway beyond the $600 million-$700 million that we think we're going to monetize out of Sky Ranch.
[Unknown Speaker 2]
Unknown Speaker 2
I look forward to that. Although my baseline comparison was always going to be the attractiveness of Sky Ranch, and I'm not expecting you to buy anything quite that attractive at this point.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
You're right about that. I hate to see the economy that leads us to what it would look like when I did acquire Sky Ranch. I understand. Yeah.
[Unknown Speaker 2]
Unknown Speaker 2
Third, in terms of I found the data center comment interesting. Where in your area are there potential locations of data centers? How does that fit in with your service area?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Great question. We've spent a bit of time working on this data center opportunities. There's a lot of money sitting, waiting for ready-to-go sites. There's three metrics for a data center. What are the property location, availability of power, and availability of water? I'd say we have the advantage that we have is we have the water side. A lot of these cities and municipalities really don't want that type of user just because it doesn't grow their AV as fast. They may end up having to commit five, seven hundred homes' worth of water to one user. That user's not going to have the same tax base as that seven hundred homes' worth would.
We have the ability of providing that water to them. We're long. It's a good allocation for us. The siting of it is less important. They can move around, but they do need to be close to water. They do need to be close to power and because of Sky Ranch's location, it really does check all those boxes. We have had conversations with specific users. We've had engagement with Cushman. They're one of the largest brokers that are managing sites for data centers. We're very optimistic that that might lead to a great opportunity for us.

Last, my question is, in your market, what's happening to price appreciation in general in the Denver market on existing homes? Two, has your first phase or maybe your first two phases been in existence long enough so that you're starting to see resales and how those resales compare to the owner's original cost?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Yeah. We are seeing great appreciation on the resales in Sky Ranch. I think that's attributable to when we broke into the market, we had a very attractive lot value, which allowed our home builders to have a very attractive home price. Some of the phase one home prices are up as much as 30%-40% since they were built, which is terrific for the community. It's terrific for those homeowners. On average, home appreciation is in that 4%-5% on a national average.
I'd say we're seeing a little bit stronger performance on that at Sky Ranch because you're getting more amenities. You're getting schools. You're getting a more mature community on that. There's less inventory at this price point. If you bought a house for $430,000, that appreciation is going to there's still no homes for sale sub-500. There's a lot of opportunity for appreciation of those homes sub-500.
[Unknown Speaker 2]
Unknown Speaker 2
That makes Sky Ranch, and that's one of the real attractions for your existing builders then, in effect.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
It is. I'd say that's why in a relatively weak market, and you can see in some of the local press where a lot of home builders are dropping a lot of projects in and around the metropolitan area, but we're getting new home builders in our existing project.
[Unknown Speaker 2]
Unknown Speaker 2
Thanks, Mark. Keep up the good work.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Thanks, Tucker. Good to hear from you.
Joakim By
Senior Portfolio Manager, Coeli Circulus
Hi, Mark and team. This is Joakim from Circles Asset Management in Stockholm, Sweden. How are you?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Great to see you.
Joakim By
Senior Portfolio Manager, Coeli Circulus
Thanks a lot. I have two questions. The first one was on the guidance range. It would be interesting to hear you elaborate a little bit around the two different, it was quite broad, outcomes. I'm saying that again. The guidance range that you provided in the area 2028, what changes?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
You know what that's going to be is really a flex into how much oil and gas we get in there. They pay us to be at their beck and call. They pay us a lot of a high rate for delivering raw water. They want a ton of water, but they go from 0 to 100 in days. Sometimes it depends on how the rig availability is. What I do know is they have all their permits lined up, and then they've constructed their pad sites. It's a matter of keeping that rig on site. I know they drilled 10 wells on one pad site. They're currently drilling, I think, another dozen wells on another pad site. We see there's some foreseeability into between 20 and 35 wells on that. That's the range on that because it is a high margin opportunity for us.
Joakim By
Senior Portfolio Manager, Coeli Circulus
Great. Thanks. The other question was around water assets. If you have seen water prices starting to creep up, and I think that's the general trend. What's the pricing on water assets right now? What would be the worth of the water if you marked it to market, so to say?
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
Yep. Great question. There's two benchmarks for that. We continue to see strength and appreciation in the TAP fees. Our TAP fees over the last, say, three or four years have increased around 6%-7% per year. We're up north of around $42,000 a year in our water and wastewater connections. When taking a look at just the straight cost per acre-foot, we bought some water in a strategic location. Our first farm that we bought in that location was about four years ago, four or five years ago. We paid about $9,700 per acre-foot for that. Most recent transactions are north of $20,000 an acre-foot. That gives you two different benchmarks, actual acre-feet purchases, as well as the strength of the service model that we have in providing service on those 60,000 connections.
Joakim By
Senior Portfolio Manager, Coeli Circulus
Okay. Thanks a lot and have a nice day.
Mark Harding
President and CEO, Pure Cycle Corporation
You too. Maybe I'll just take a second too. I know you got. I don't know if you were asking specifically about our guidance in fiscal 2028, where that's coming from, but a lot of what we're projecting after the interchange in 2027 is the ability to sell some of that commercial along with phase III. When we add the capacity to Sky Ranch, our lot revenue will really be able to scale as long as the market holds it with some commercial lots as additional to some home lots.
In 2025, 2026, we're just selling residential lots in sub-phases in order to stay within our capacity limits of the interchange. What we see in 2028 and beyond is the ability to do residential as well as commercial. I don't know if that was specifically what your question was related to, but that's really the big change that you see in some of the guidance that we're expecting in the future. I don't know if you want to comment on that or.
Marc Spezialy
